basis: Cerebellar vermis malformation, posterior fossa cyst and hydrocephalus define the disease; skull shape changes do not establish separate skeletal damage.
Childhood melanoma predominantly originates in cutaneous melanocytes; rare leptomeningeal subtypes do not determine umbrella labels.
Congenital nephrosis and ocular anomalies define Pierson syndrome; developmental delay occurs in 30-79%, with microcephaly in 3/4 annotated patients.
Steroid-induced glaucoma directly damages the ocular optic nerve; the treatment-related cause does not alter the disease's primary location.
Inherited retinal degeneration caused by PDE6C variants; no extraocular disease is established.
Bidirectional ventricular tachycardia is a cardiac rhythm disorder; underlying causes are separate conditions.
Immune-mediated muscle and skin disease; interstitial lung disease directly affects roughly 30% or more, with prevalence varying across adult cohorts.
Sarcoma originates in the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ outside the axes; sarcoma histology alone does not establish locomotor involvement.
Isolated spermatogenic failure with acephalic spermatozoa and infertility; no endocrine dysfunction or other axis involvement is established.
Named syndrome comprises cerebral calcifications, abnormal opalescent teeth and renal phosphate wasting; absent definition and phenotypes limit certainty.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability characterize the deletion umbrella; other organ defects depend on the deleted region.
Thecoma arises from ovarian steroidogenic theca cells, representing the endocrine component of the gonad.
Inherited temporal and occipital lobe epilepsy; visual aura and auditory hallucinations are cerebral phenomena, not eye or ear damage.
Bone fragility, recurrent fractures and skeletal deformity define the disease; blue sclerae do not establish ocular dysfunction, and motor delay is skeletal.
Defined by disrupted organic acid metabolism; the broad concept does not establish common damage to a specific additional organ.
Hereditary congenital eyelid ptosis; compensatory chin elevation does not establish a separate neurologic or skeletal disorder.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss in 8/8 annotated patients; the PCDH15 gene does not justify importing Usher syndrome features.
Nonsyndromic prelingual sensorineural hearing loss in 6/6 annotated patients; no retinal or other extra-aural damage is established.
Chronic suppurative middle-ear infection causes persistent tympanic perforation and conductive hearing loss; preceding respiratory infections are separate.
An inherited pentose phosphate pathway enzyme deficiency causing red-cell dysfunction and hemolytic anemia.
Caudal skeletal/neural defect; bowel dysfunction 80-99%, anal atresia and urinary malformations 30-79%. Cardiovascular anomalies (30-79%) omitted under the four-axis cap.
Acquired proximal tubular dysfunction is defined by solute wasting, including phosphate and bicarbonate, producing electrolyte and acid-base abnormalities.
Congenital unilateral fusion of the humerus, radius and ulna directly affects bones and elbow mobility.
IgA-mediated glomerular injury defines the disease; hypertension is occasional, while cirrhosis and celiac disease are separate associated conditions.
Alcohol-induced inflammatory liver injury; inflammation alone does not make this an autoimmune or infectious disease.
